creator: Alexander Terp
description:
SwiftPM cannot import an executable target into a test target, so every line in Sources/muster is unreachable by the suite. Real decisions are sitting there today: PaneInput (keymap, then encode, then deliver), paneCommand, the launch sequencing, and the keyDown arbitration between an input method and the key encoder.

That last one shipped a bug that doubled every printable keystroke - insertText and the encoder both sent it - and no test could have caught it, because no test can reach the file. It was found by a human typing 'hello' and reading 'hheelllloo'.

The desideratum already says it: a thin shell over a thick headless core, so no logic hides in the untestable layer. main.swift stopped being thin.

Move each piece into a library target and unit-test it. The arbitration is the valuable one and is pure: given (was composing, what insertText committed, whether marked text remains), decide send-text, send-key, or send-nothing. Five lines of test would have caught the doubling.

NSEvent translation goes with it. NSEvent.keyEvent(with:...) is a plain constructor - no app, no window, no run loop - so KeyTranslation.swift's ported heuristics are table-testable today and are currently tested by nothing at all.
title: No decidable logic may live in the executable target
